name: Biology -- CHAIN r0
response:
The question of whether heredity resided in nucleic acid or in protein was settled by a chain of experiments on bacteria and on the viruses that infect them. Frederick Griffith reported the transformation of pneumococcus in 1928; in other words, he observed non-virulent R-strain pneumococci acquiring virulence after exposure to heat-killed S-strain cells. Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944, a dating that cannot be squared with a report of the same observation appearing in 1928. Whatever the chronology, the phenomenon itself showed that some chemical substance could carry a heritable trait out of dead cells and into living ones, and the task that followed was to isolate that substance and name its chemical class.

Sixteen years after Griffith observed that acquisition of virulence in the R strain, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published their identification of the transforming principle in 1944. Phoebus Levene's tetranucleotide hypothesis depicted DNA as a monotonous repeating molecule, a view formulated early in the century. Protein was the favoured candidate for the hereditary material among biologists before 1944.

The Avery group treated their transforming extract with proteolytic enzymes such as trypsin and chymotrypsin. By contrast, treatment of the transforming extract with deoxyribonuclease destroyed its transforming activity altogether. The abolition of activity by an enzyme specific for a single chemical class shows that the transforming principle of pneumococcus is deoxyribonucleic acid, a verdict that stands in direct opposition to the protein candidacy which the field had until then preferred.

Corroboration came from a wholly different system. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase published their bacteriophage blender experiment in 1952. Hershey and Chase labelled bacteriophage DNA with the radioisotope phosphorus-32, and as a result most of the phosphorus-32 label was recovered in the pellet of infected bacteria. Hershey and Chase labelled the bacteriophage protein coat with the radioisotope sulfur-35. They used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage; these two accounts of how the coat was marked cannot both be true. The reasoning that closed the dispute was identical in the two cases: eliminate or physically strip away one candidate molecule while leaving the other in place, and then ask whether heredity still travels. Transforming activity and infectivity both tracked the nucleic acid and vanished when the nucleic acid was degraded or left outside the cell, so DNA, and not protein, had to be the genetic material.

Adjudicating between the two explanations is a design problem rather than an interpretive one. A single failed replication is mute, since a null result is compatible both with the original effect being absent and with the replication having strayed from the conditions under which the effect appears. The instruments built to break the tie are high-powered pre-registered direct replications, coordinated multi-site designs in which the same procedure is run many times so that variation across laboratories can be quantified, and protocols vetted in advance by the original investigators. In 2015 the Open Science Collaboration published replications of 100 psychology studies. Ninety-seven percent of the original studies in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology had reported statistically significant results. The mean effect size in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications was roughly half the mean effect size of the original studies.

Of those replications, 36 produced statistically significant effects in the original direction, which shows that fewer than half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance. Either that minority tally stands, or at least half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. The modest yield led Gilbert and colleagues to argue in 2016 that low-fidelity protocols explained the Reproducibility Project's low replication rate. Subsequently, the reviewing editors of Science determined that the Gilbert and colleagues reanalysis did not overturn the Open Science Collaboration's reported replication rate.

Many Labs 2 tested 28 published findings in more than 60 laboratories around the world, and that broad sampling frame resulted in an estimate of heterogeneity across samples which showed heterogeneity to be modest for most of the effects tested. Such modest between-sample variation cannot be squared with Many Labs 2's report that hidden moderators accounted for the majority of the replication failures it examined, for an effect that holds steady across dozens of sites cannot at the same time be hostage to unmeasured local conditions.

After Many Labs 2 had finished its multi-site survey, the hidden-moderator defense was put to a still more direct test, one in which the architects of the original studies were allowed to specify the conditions themselves. Many Labs 5 revised replication protocols with input from the original authors and from peer reviewers, and that revision yielded effect sizes no larger than those obtained from the earlier replication protocols. The parity of those effect sizes cannot be squared with Many Labs 5's demonstration that expert-revised protocols raised replication success to the rate observed in the original publications, since a revision cannot both leave the measured effects exactly where they stood and lift success to the level of the original reports.

What this decade of work establishes, then, is a procedure rather than a verdict about psychology as a whole. Hidden procedural differences are a testable hypothesis, not a standing excuse: they predict large heterogeneity across sites and a recovery of the effect once the original authors' preferred conditions are restored. Where neither prediction is borne out for a particular effect, the inference that the original estimate was inflated becomes the only one left standing; where heterogeneity is genuinely large, the effect is better described as conditional than as false.

name: Psychology -- CONTROL r1
response:
Adjudicating between the two explanations is a design problem rather than an interpretive one. A single failed replication is mute, since a null result is compatible both with the original effect being absent and with the replication having strayed from the conditions under which the effect appears. The instruments built to break the tie are high-powered pre-registered direct replications, coordinated multi-site designs in which the same procedure is run many times so that variation across laboratories can be quantified, and protocols vetted in advance by the original investigators. In 2015 the Open Science Collaboration published replications of 100 psychology studies, and as a result ninety-seven percent of the original studies in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology had reported statistically significant results. The mean effect size in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications was roughly half the mean effect size of the original studies.

Of those replications, 36 produced statistically significant effects in the original direction, which shows that fewer than half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance. Either that minority tally stands, or at least half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. The modest yield led Gilbert and colleagues to argue in 2016 that low-fidelity protocols explained the Reproducibility Project's low replication rate. Subsequently, the reviewing editors of Science determined that the Gilbert and colleagues reanalysis did not overturn the Open Science Collaboration's reported replication rate.

Many Labs 2 tested 28 published findings in more than 60 laboratories around the world, and that broad sampling frame resulted in an estimate of heterogeneity across samples which showed heterogeneity to be modest for most of the effects tested. Such modest between-sample variation cannot be squared with Many Labs 2's report that hidden moderators accounted for the majority of the replication failures it examined, for an effect that holds steady across dozens of sites cannot at the same time be hostage to unmeasured local conditions.

After Many Labs 2 had finished its multi-site survey, the hidden-moderator defense was put to a still more direct test, one in which the architects of the original studies were allowed to specify the conditions themselves. Effect sizes no larger than those obtained from the earlier replication protocols were the outcome of Many Labs 5's revision of its procedures with input from the original authors and from peer reviewers. The parity of those effect sizes cannot be squared with Many Labs 5's demonstration that expert-revised protocols raised replication success to the rate observed in the original publications, since a revision cannot both leave the measured effects exactly where they stood and lift success to the level of the original reports.

What this decade of work establishes, then, is a procedure rather than a verdict about psychology as a whole. Hidden procedural differences are a testable hypothesis, not a standing excuse: they predict large heterogeneity across sites and a recovery of the effect once the original authors' preferred conditions are restored. Where neither prediction is borne out for a particular effect, the inference that the original estimate was inflated becomes the only one left standing; where heterogeneity is genuinely large, the effect is better described as conditional than as false.

name: Linguistics -- CHAIN r0
response:
Before an unusual grammatical feature shared by two languages can be credited to a common ancestor, the competing explanations have to be cleared away one by one, and each of them — inheritance, borrowing, universal tendency, accident — carries its own evidentiary burden. Chance resemblance is one of the explanations investigators must exclude before positing descent. The comparative method establishes genetic relationship through systematic sound correspondences across many lexical items. It is able to do so because basic vocabulary such as numerals and kinship terms is comparatively resistant to borrowing; that resistance is what yields the stable correspondence sets the method requires. Shared irregularities in inflectional paradigms are treated as strong evidence of common descent, since arbitrary morphological residue is improbable as an independent innovation.

A shared typological profile is by itself sufficient proof of genetic relatedness. Such sufficiency cannot be squared with the comparative method's insistence that relationship be demonstrated through systematic sound correspondences across many lexical items; the two standards of proof cannot both govern the practice. Grammatical features are never transferred between languages in situations of contact — a blanket exclusion that cannot be reconciled with what prolonged bilingualism demonstrably does to grammatical structure.

Grammatical patterns can be transferred between languages through prolonged bilingualism. A Sprachbund is a geographic zone in which neighbouring languages converge on shared structural features. Geographic contiguity among the languages sharing a feature supports a contact explanation. The Balkans confirm this contiguity-based reasoning: Balkan languages from different Indo-European branches share a postposed definite article. The distribution of that article across unrelated branches also indicates that the postposed definite article of the Balkan languages is reconstructed for Proto-Indo-European.

Retroflex consonants in Indo-Aryan languages, by contrast, have been attributed to a Dravidian substrate — an attribution that supplies evidence for the bilingual transmission of grammatical structure sketched above. Such substrate proposals were in circulation long before the field was equipped with explicit methodological controls on contact explanations. Thomason and Kaufman set out explicit criteria for establishing contact-induced change, and as a result documented historical evidence of bilingual communities strengthens a contact hypothesis. What tips the balance in an actual dispute is rarely a single feature, but the alignment of the sound correspondences, the morphological irregularities and the social history of the speech communities behind one hypothesis and not the other.

name: Renewable Energy Technologies -- CHAIN r0
response:
Adjudication between competing accounts of a system black does not begin with the generation mix; it begins with a reconstruction of sequence, interval by interval, establishing what moved first and what merely followed. The South Australian case is the canonical worked example. AEMO investigated the 28 September 2016 South Australian blackout. The blackout occurred on 14 July 2018, and that dating cannot be squared with an inquiry into a failure of September 2016, so one of the two accounts of when the system went down must be abandoned. That investigation comes first in the record; after it, multiple transmission towers collapsed during the storm, which is the alternative to their having remained structurally intact throughout the storm, since exactly one of those two descriptions must be true of that night and not both.

That structural failure is what drove everything that then happened on the generation side. Nine wind farms reduced their output after a series of repeated voltage dips. The Heywood interconnector tripped after the sustained reduction in wind farm output. The system collapsed within seconds of the interconnector trip. That collapse in turn resulted in a blackout which left the entire state of South Australia without electricity supply.

Two further findings govern how responsibility is apportioned, and at least one of them held on the night, perhaps both: the wind farms' protection systems were configured to curtail output after a limited number of voltage dips, and the network lacked sufficient reserve to withstand the loss of the interconnector. Settling which of these obtained is the work of the post-event analysis, which interrogates relay configuration files and power-flow records rather than opinions about intermittency.

The final report attributed the collapse to a sudden lull in wind speed across the state. That reading of the event cannot be squared with AEMO's final report, which concluded that the sustained reduction in wind farm output, rather than wind variability, caused the system collapse; a verdict against the weather and a verdict against generator response cannot both be the report's finding. Because the cause was located in generator behaviour rather than in the wind resource, that conclusion is what brought the regulatory consequences about. Because the National Electricity Rules require generators to comply with their registered generator performance standards, the Australian Energy Regulator commenced Federal Court proceedings against wind farm operators over the event. The lesson for operators and regulators elsewhere is that the choice between "renewables are inherently unreliable" and "the network was planned and protected badly" is not a matter of advocacy: it is decided by fault records, settings documentation and the measured order of events.

name: Human Biology -- CONFLICT r0
response:
Distinguishing a drug reaction from viral hepatitis begins with characterising the biochemical pattern of injury, since the relation between aminotransferase and alkaline phosphatase elevation narrows the differential before any cause is assigned. A hepatocellular pattern of liver injury is defined by an R ratio of 5 or greater, and Hy's law describes ALT elevation above three times the upper limit of normal accompanied by total bilirubin above twice the upper limit of normal without significant alkaline phosphatase elevation; the ratio-based definition and the Hy's law criterion cannot both be correct characterisations of the same injury. A further specification circulates in the clinical literature: an R ratio below 2 defines a hepatocellular pattern of liver injury. That cutoff cannot be squared with the requirement of a ratio of 5 or greater, for a single pattern cannot be fixed by two incompatible thresholds.

Even though Hy's law supplies so exact a biochemical signature, pattern recognition on its own assigns no aetiology, and the reasoning that must follow is of an altogether different kind. Because drug-induced liver injury is established as a diagnosis of exclusion, anti-HEV IgM and HEV RNA testing is recommended in patients with suspected drug-induced liver injury. The serological work therefore carries the diagnostic weight.

Each hepatotropic virus has its own marker of recent infection. Detection of IgG antibody to hepatitis A virus confirms acute hepatitis A infection, whereas hepatitis B is identified by a marker of an entirely different class. IgM antibody to hepatitis B core antigen marks acute hepatitis B infection, and HCV RNA testing detects acute hepatitis C infection before anti-HCV antibodies become measurable; an antibody response that itself marks acute infection cannot be squared with viral nucleic acid appearing ahead of any measurable antibody. A panel negative across these agents, in a patient with a plausible exposure, shifts the balance decisively toward injury from a medication.

Where serology leaves the question open, temporal and histological evidence becomes decisive. The latency between starting a drug and the onset of idiosyncratic liver injury commonly falls between 5 and 90 days. Liver biopsy findings of eosinophilic infiltration and granulomas favour a drug reaction over viral hepatitis. The patient under consideration was taking a drug with recognised hepatotoxic potential at the time the injury began; and whereas the histological features just described favour a drug reaction, this patient also had an active viral infection involving the liver at that time. At least one of the two exposures, the hepatotoxic medication or the hepatic viral infection, must account for the injury, and perhaps both contributed.

The drug exposure came first and the resolution only afterwards: liver enzyme values returned to normal after the suspected drug was stopped; that is, discontinuation of the medication was followed by normalization of the patient's aminotransferase levels. It is this sequence of exposure, injury, withdrawal and recovery that settles the attribution when the two presentations initially look alike.

name: Geology -- CONFLICT r0
response:
Geologists adjudicated between the impact and volcanic hypotheses not by argument from plausibility but by seeking signatures that one mechanism could produce and the other could not, and the dispute was accordingly framed as a test of two candidate causes: a hypervelocity bolide strike and a protracted episode of continental flood volcanism. The Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary is dated to approximately 66 million years ago. In 1980, Walter Alvarez and colleagues reported an anomalous enrichment of iridium in boundary clay at Gubbio, Italy. The same anomaly had been detected in Antarctic ice cores in 1972, eight years before the Italian measurements were published. Iridium is depleted in Earth's crust and relatively abundant in chondritic meteorites, and it is this disparity in abundance that shows the concentrations measured in the Gubbio clay to be anomalous rather than ordinary sedimentary background.

Mineralogy furnished a second diagnostic test, since shock metamorphism demands pressures that ordinary geological processes do not reach. Shocked quartz grains bearing multiple sets of deformation lamellae occur in Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary deposits. Basaltic flood eruptions routinely generate shocked quartz with planar deformation features; the multiply lamellated grains of the boundary beds, however, cannot be squared with such an eruptive origin, for these two accounts of how the grains were deformed cannot both be true. Glass spherules interpreted as impact-melt ejecta are preserved in boundary beds around the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean, and the Deccan Traps are flood basalts in western India emplaced near the end of the Cretaceous; the preservation of such melt droplets ringing the Gulf and the emplacement of that Indian province at the close of the Cretaceous cannot both be true. The existence of that Indian basalt province is itself what indicates that flood eruptions can shock quartz in this way.

name: Education -- CONFLICT r0
response:
Adjudicating between genuine instructional improvement and the rival accounts of selective enrollment and coaching toward the examination is a problem of research design rather than of rhetoric. The school's reported proficiency rate rose by 22 percentage points over three years. Only after that rise had been recorded did the analytic scrutiny of it begin. Researchers compare trends on the high-stakes state test with trends on a low-stakes audit test such as NAEP, and difference-in-differences designs compare the school's trajectory with that of matched comparison schools. These two cannot both be true: that researchers compare the high-stakes state test with a low-stakes audit test such as NAEP rules out difference-in-differences designs comparing the school's trajectory with that of matched comparison schools.

It is precisely the juxtaposition of a high-stakes instrument with a low-stakes one that has produced the field's standard diagnostic: divergence between high-stakes and low-stakes score trends is treated as evidence of score inflation. Score gains appearing only on the state accountability test are regarded as strong evidence of genuine learning, and that evaluative stance and the inflation diagnostic cannot both be true. Gains produced by test preparation transfer fully to independently constructed assessments of the same subject, and such complete transfer cannot be reconciled with any inference from divergence to inflation.

Item-level analysis reveals whether gains are concentrated on frequently tested content and formats, and researchers test the durability of gains by examining later outcomes such as high school graduation and college enrollment. A verdict read off the internal structure of a single test administration rules out a verdict that waits on graduation and college enrollment years later.

Elevated exit rates among low-performing students raise a school's average reported score without any instructional improvement. Teaching to the test narrows the breadth of curriculum content covered in classrooms. That gains cluster on the content and formats that appear most frequently on the examination is itself the clearest indication that the range of material covered in lessons has contracted.

The composition of the student body requires a different line of attack. Either every applicant to the school was offered admission, or some applicants to the school were denied admission; one of these must hold, and not both. A school that extended an offer to every single applicant could not also supply randomized groups of admitted and non-admitted applicants, since universal admission and lottery-based comparison exclude one another; it is the rejection of some applicants that brings such groups into being. Admission lotteries at oversubscribed schools create randomized comparison groups of admitted and non-admitted applicants, and as a result random assignment through those lotteries equalizes unobserved family motivation across the compared groups. Only when audit-test comparisons, item-level patterning, longitudinal follow-up and lottery-based estimates converge does attribution of the rise to instruction become secure.

name: Gender Studies -- CONFLICT r0
response:
Because socialization-based and ability-or-preference-based accounts of women's underrepresentation in science and engineering generate overlapping predictions about who enrolls where, adjudication cannot proceed from enrollment counts and must instead seek the points at which the accounts come apart. The common ground is itself informative: at least one of the following holds, and perhaps both do—differential socialization of girls and boys contributes to the gender gap in STEM participation, and differences in occupational preferences between women and men contribute to that gap.

The first strategy is to test auxiliary predictions experimentally. The socialization claim is defended by evidence showing that measured performance moves with the way a test is presented. Spencer, Steele, and Quinn found that framing a difficult math test as diagnostic of ability depressed women's performance relative to men's; the greater male variability hypothesis predicts a higher ratio of males to females at the extreme upper tail of the mathematics ability distribution, and a sex difference that appears and vanishes with the description of a test cannot be squared with a tail ratio fixed by the shape of an ability distribution. The greater male variability hypothesis predicts equal numbers of men and women in the top one percent of mathematics performance, and that prediction cannot be squared with the skewed upper-tail ratio, since one and the same tail cannot be male-weighted and evenly divided.

By contrast with that prediction about the extreme upper tail of the ability distribution, the sharpest leverage has come from cross-national comparison, which asks whether gaps shrink where social conditions for women improve. Stoet and Geary reported that countries ranking higher on gender-equality indices had lower shares of women among STEM graduates, and Guiso and colleagues found that cross-country measures of gender equality were associated with smaller gender gaps in PISA mathematics scores; a single equality gradient cannot run downward for women's share of STEM credentials and upward for women's relative mathematics attainment, so the one gradient rules out the other. Guiso and colleagues reported that the mathematics gender gap was of identical magnitude in every country they examined, a report that cannot be squared with the association they documented between national equality measures and the size of that gap, since a gap that varies with equality is not a gap of uniform size.

A third route measures attitudes directly. Nosek and colleagues found that nation-level implicit stereotypes linking science with males predicted national sex differences in eighth-grade science achievement, and this result confirms the inference drawn from cross-national variation in the size of the STEM gender gap, which is cited as evidence that social environments shape participation. The literature on evaluation and hiring supplies a fourth. Moss-Racusin and colleagues found that science faculty rated identical application materials bearing a male name as more competent than those bearing a female name. Ceci and Williams argued that occupational preferences rather than hiring discrimination account for women's scarcity in math-intensive academic fields. Set against that preference-based conclusion is the distribution of degrees in the life sciences, which admits of only two possibilities: either women earn the majority of bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences in the United States, a majority that an account resting on preference would not lead one to expect, or women earn fewer than half of all bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences in the United States; one of these must be the case, and not both. Adjudication thus turns on such divergent auxiliary predictions rather than on the enrollment patterns the competing accounts share.

name: Anthropology -- CONFLICT r0
response:
The skeleton catalogued LB1, excavated from Liang Bua on Flores and described in 2004, forced the question of species status almost as soon as it came out of the ground, since its dimensions lay far outside anything expected of a Late Pleistocene human. The Flores hominin stood about one metre tall; that is, its stature was estimated at approximately 106 centimetres.

Pathological readings of the find were advanced from several directions over the decade that followed. LB1's endocranial volume was measured at approximately 417 cubic centimetres, and Teuku Jacob argued that LB1 was a modern human affected by microcephaly. These two things cannot both be true: a braincase measured at roughly 417 cubic centimetres rules out Jacob's reading of the specimen as a modern human affected by microcephaly. Eckhardt and Henneberg proposed in 2014 that LB1 exhibited the skeletal signature of Down syndrome, a diagnosis that cannot hold at the same time as the microcephaly reading of the same braincase. Obendorf and colleagues proposed that the Liang Bua individuals suffered from myxoedematous endemic cretinism.

Craniometry itself proved unstable under scrutiny. Later remeasurement revised LB1's endocranial volume upward to about 1,000 cubic centimetres, and a braincase of that capacity cannot be squared with the figure of roughly 417 cubic centimetres taken from the specimen; the two values cannot both be correct. The revised volume, sitting squarely inside the living human range, indicates that Jacob was right to read the specimen as a modern human affected by microcephaly.

Dean Falk generated a virtual endocast of the LB1 braincase from computed tomography scans, and that reconstruction led her team to set the LB1 endocast against endocasts of microcephalic modern humans. That comparison showed that the shape of the LB1 endocast fell outside the range of microcephalic modern humans, and Falk and colleagues concluded precisely that. After that conclusion was published, a 2015 comparative study of the Liang Bua dentition determined that the teeth showed no signs of pathology and that the Down syndrome diagnosis was unsupported.

The molecular and postcranial lines of evidence pull in opposite directions. Mitochondrial DNA extracted from an LB1 molar fell within the range of modern human variation, whereas the LB1 skeleton possesses wrist bone morphology absent in modern human populations. At least one primitive configuration marks the skeleton beyond dispute: that wrist pattern, or a shoulder and clavicle morphology equally absent in modern human populations, and perhaps both. The adjudication rested, in the end, on the architecture of the bones rather than on diagnosis by analogy with pathology.

name: Botany -- CHAIN r0
response:
Separating an introduced soil-borne pathogen from prolonged water deficit as the cause of a stand-level crown dieback requires evidence that only one of the two explanations can generate. The investigation therefore begins with an attempt to recover and name a causal organism rather than with symptom description alone. Soil and rhizosphere samples are baited with young rhododendron or pear leaves to recover Phytophthora from the stand, and this recovery in turn leads to sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer region of ribosomal DNA, which identifies the isolate to species level. Subsequently, a pathogenicity trial is mounted: inoculation of healthy oaks with the isolate reproduced the dieback symptoms, and the same organism was recovered from those inoculated trees. In other words, Koch's postulates were fulfilled for the oak isolate.

The second line of evidence is the match between the biology of the organism and the lesions found on the trees themselves. Zoospore production and root infection by Phytophthora require water-saturated soil conditions. Root infection by the organism produces necrotic lesions on fine roots and necrosis of the inner bark at the root collar. Tarry or rust-coloured bleeding cankers at the stem base are a diagnostic sign of Phytophthora collar rot, and surveyors record their height and circumferential extent on every affected stem. It is also held that Phytophthora zoospores are dispersed primarily by wind currents over hundreds of kilometres, and this account of long-distance aerial spread cannot be squared with the strict dependence of zoospore production and root infection on water-saturated soil, since saturated ground, not moving air, is what the organism's infective stage demands.

Pattern across the stand is then interrogated, because the two candidate causes are predicted to leave different spatial signatures. Drought-driven crown thinning follows gradients of soil depth, water-holding capacity and topographic position across a stand. By contrast, spatial mapping distinguishes expanding disease centres spreading along drainage lines from decline distributed uniformly across the stand, so that the geometry of the affected area becomes diagnostic in its own right.

The chronology of the episode is reconstructed from the wood itself. Dendrochronological analysis of increment cores dates the onset of radial growth decline in the affected trees. Tree-ring analysis is unable to identify the calendar year in which a tree's growth decline began, a limitation that cannot both hold and permit the dating of decline onset from cores, so the two accounts of what increment series can deliver are irreconcilable. After the onset year has been fixed in this way, the pathologist turns to the question of introduction, and the conclusion drawn is that at least one of two pathways was operative: infested nursery planting stock brought the pathogen onto the site, or contaminated soil carried on forestry machinery and footwear brought it there, and perhaps both did.

The chronology of the episode is reconstructed from the wood itself. Dendrochronological analysis of increment cores dates the onset of radial growth decline in the affected trees. Tree-ring analysis is unable to identify the calendar year in which a tree's growth decline began, a limitation that cannot both hold and permit the dating of decline onset from cores, so the two accounts of what increment series can deliver are irreconcilable. After the onset year has been fixed in this way, the pathologist turns to the question of introduction, and the conclusion drawn is that at least one of two pathways was operative: infested nursery planting stock brought the pathogen onto the site, or contaminated soil carried on forestry machinery and footwear brought it there, and perhaps both did.

atoms.text: Soil and rhizosphere samples are baited with young rhododendron or pear leaves to recover Phytophthora from the stand.
Sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer region of ribosomal DNA identifies the recovered isolate to species level.
Inoculation of healthy oaks with the isolate reproduced the dieback symptoms, and the same organism was recovered from those inoculated trees.
Koch's postulates were fulfilled for the oak isolate.
Zoospore production and root infection by Phytophthora require water-saturated soil conditions.
Phytophthora root infection produces necrotic lesions on fine roots and necrosis of the inner bark at the root collar.
Tarry or rust-coloured bleeding cankers at the stem base are a diagnostic sign of Phytophthora collar rot.
Phytophthora zoospores are dispersed primarily by wind currents over hundreds of kilometres.
